title: BTO Flat Applicants who Purchased Flats as Fiancé and Fiancée but Do Not Subsequently Submit Marriage Certificate
what_it_is: BTO Flat Applicants who Purchased Flats as Fiancé and Fiancée but Do Not Subsequently Submit Marriage Certificate

sections.label: HDB fiancé-fiancée marriage certificate tracking
sections.summary: HDB does not track fiancé-fiancée flat applicants who submitted their marriage certificate after six months of taking possession.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB does not track the number of fiancé-fiancée flat applicants who submitted their marriage certificate after six months of taking possession of their flat.

sections.label: Outstanding fiancé-fiancée flat cases
sections.summary: As of 31 December 2022, 79 couples had not produced marriage certificates; HDB allowed three retentions, began two acquisitions, and five applied to surrender.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As of 31 December 2022, there were 79 couples who have bought their new flats from HDB under the Fiancé-Fiancée Scheme in the last 10 years and have taken possession of their flats for more than six months but have yet to produce their marriage certificate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Of these 79 couples, HDB allowed three of the cases to have one of the applicants retain the flat with the inclusion of a family member originally listed in the flat application and initiated compulsory acquisition actions against two of them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Another five couples have submitted applications to surrender their flats.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB will continue to work with the owners of the remaining outstanding cases to regularise their lease through the submission of marriage certificate, surrender of the flat or via compulsory acquisition actions.

sections.label: Break-up breaches flat eligibility condition
sections.summary: A fiancé-fiancée break-up breaches the family nucleus eligibility condition; HDB compulsorily acquires flats unless one party retains with originally listed parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Essentially, with a break-up of the fiancé-fiancée relationship, there is a breach of the fundamental eligibility condition of the family nucleus to buy a flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If the flat owners refuse to surrender, then, of course, HDB will compulsorily acquire the flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And then, specific to the question that Assoc Prof Lim raised, the only exception to allow one party to retain the flat is with parents who were originally listed in the application for purchase of the flat, as the retaining party with his or her parents would have qualified to buy the flat as a family nucleus even without the couple's marriage.
